text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Islamist-led government plans to give financial support to Islamist press while trying to censure secularist media.
- Kurdish rebels release six Turkish soldiers held hostage in northern Iraq for 18 months.
- Leading Turkish businessmen go to Athens on trip that is example to squabbling politicians.
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan under pressure from grassroots supporters to clean up security scandal.
- Then prime minister Tansu Ciller allegedly gave 250 billion lira from slush fund to far-right gangsters to kill Kurdish rebel chief Abdullah Ocalan in 1994.
- Iraqi oil expected to flow through pipeline to Turkey on Tuesday.
- Treasury official says conditions good for foreign borrowing.
- Erbakan aims to replace around 50 provincial governors with associates.
- People lose faith in system because of security scandal.
